question_text: How should you file the names 'Perez-Gomez, Luis' and 'Perez, Maria'?

hint_ladder.title: Hint 1
hint_ladder.text: Think about how filing rules treat hyphenated last names. Are they considered one name or two separate names?

hint_ladder.title: Hint 2
hint_ladder.text: Hyphenated surnames are treated as a single unit. So 'Perez-Gomez' is one last name, not 'Perez' and 'Gomez' separately.

hint_ladder.title: Hint 3
hint_ladder.text: Now compare 'Perez' and 'Perez-Gomez' letter by letter. They start the same: P-e-r-e-z. After 'z', the name 'Perez' ends (which is like a space or nothing), while 'Perez-Gomez' continues with a hyphen. In alphabetical order, a space (end of name) comes before a hyphen.

hint_ladder.title: Hint 4
hint_ladder.text: So 'Perez' comes first because it's shorter and ends before the hyphenated name continues. That means 'Perez, Maria' should be filed before 'Perez-Gomez, Luis'.

A.text: This is the correct order. 'Perez' is a shorter surname that ends after the sixth letter, while 'Perez-Gomez' continues with a hyphen. Since a space (end of name) comes before a hyphen alphabetically, 'Perez' is filed first.

B.text: This puts 'Perez-Gomez' before 'Perez', but that's like putting 'Smith-Jones' before 'Smith'. The shorter name always comes first when they start the same way. A smart guess, but the hyphen doesn't give priority.

C.text: This splits the hyphenated surname into two separate names, filing 'Gomez' as the last name. That's a common mistake, but hyphenated names stay together as one unit. You wouldn't file 'Smith-Jones' under 'Jones'.

D.text: This also breaks the hyphenated name apart and treats 'Gomez' as the surname for both people. Remember, 'Perez-Gomez' is a single last name, so it stays whole.

deconstruct_text: Let's walk through this filing problem step by step. First, remember the golden rule: hyphenated surnames are treated as one complete unit. So 'Perez-Gomez' is a single last name, not two separate names. Now, to file alphabetically, compare 'Perez' and 'Perez-Gomez' letter by letter. Both start with P-e-r-e-z. After the 'z', the name 'Perez' ends -- think of that as a space or nothing. Meanwhile, 'Perez-Gomez' continues with a hyphen. In alphabetical order, a space comes before a hyphen. That means 'Perez' is filed first. So the correct sequence is 'Perez, Maria' followed by 'Perez-Gomez, Luis'. The mental trick here is the 'Space Before Hyphen' rule: when two names start the same, the shorter one (ending in a space) always comes before the longer one with a hyphen.
next_time_rule: Space Before Hyphen: When two surnames start with the same letters, the shorter one (ending with a space) comes before the longer hyphenated one. Hyphenated names stay whole.
